sources.title: É. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, Lecture Notes in Physics 846 (2012; author preprint arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1)
sources.locator: Full 220-page PDF retrieved. Inspected §2.4 equation (2.43) for the extrinsic-curvature sign; §6.3.3 equations (6.48)–(6.52); §§6.4.1–6.4.2 equations (6.53), (6.79)–(6.83); §§6.5.2–6.5.3 equations (6.101)–(6.104); and §§8.2.2–8.2.4 equations (8.5)–(8.8), including surrounding derivations.

contents.name: §2.4, equation (2.43): extrinsic-curvature sign convention
contents.reason: This records Gourgoulhon’s opposite sign for K; the local proof follows the library convention and derives the momentum formula from that convention.

contents.name: §6.3.3, equations (6.48)–(6.52): conformal scalar-curvature transformation
contents.support: The source gives the scalar transformation; the item independently derives it from the Christoffel difference and tracks the library curvature sign.

contents.name: §6.4.1: trace and trace-free decomposition of the extrinsic curvature
contents.support: Supports the trace-free free-data split; the local definition fixes its covariant tensor convention and states the trace explicitly.

contents.name: §6.4.2, equations (6.79)–(6.83): transverse-traceless data and conformal momentum weight
contents.support: Supports the TT conformal-data route; the local proof independently derives the raised-index weight and cancellation in the momentum constraint.

contents.name: §6.5.2: Hamiltonian and momentum projections
contents.support: Supports the constraint residual conventions; the library K sign is stated and used throughout the local definition.

contents.name: §6.5.3, equations (6.101)–(6.104): conformal Hamiltonian and momentum equations
contents.support: The source supplies the transformed equations; the item gives their complete local derivation and equivalence.

contents.name: §§8.2.2–8.2.4, equations (8.5)–(8.8): CMC Lichnerowicz equation and discussion
contents.support: Supplies the CMC scalar equation used for the exact constant-coefficient specialization; the twelfth-root solution and uniqueness are derived locally.

contents.name: §§8.2.2–8.2.4: specialization to nonzero constant TT data on a flat torus
contents.support: The conformal equation supplies the source model; the TT tensor, its norm, curvature and exact constraint solution are verified directly in the example.

contents.name: §§8.2.2–8.2.4: specialization to vanishing TT data and mean curvature
contents.support: The source equation is specialized locally to the zero-data torus case; nonuniqueness and the zero Fourier mode are proved by the example itself.

source_review.read_extent: Full PDF body retrieved; every listed subsection and its surrounding derivation inspected in the full-text rendering.
source_review.supports: Conformal scalar curvature, the covariant TT split, constraint equations, CMC Lichnerowicz equation, and the source’s K sign convention for the listed local items.
source_review.limitations: Gourgoulhon uses the opposite sign for K in equation (2.43); the Hamiltonian quadratic expression is unchanged, and the local momentum proof derives the result using the library convention. No global solvability or uniqueness claim is taken from the source.

contents.support: Supports the vacuum CMC free-data formulation; local definitions fix the library covariant sigma and K conventions.

contents.name: §4.1, equations (47)–(55): conformal constraint transformations
contents.support: Provides an independent treatment of the conformal equation; the local proof supplies the complete scalar, norm and momentum derivations.

contents.name: §4.1, equations (55)–(56): CMC Lichnerowicz scalar equation
contents.support: The CMC formula is specialized to the stated constant seed data and solved by an exact positive twelfth root in the local proof.

contents.name: §4.1, CMC equation applied to nonzero flat-torus TT data
contents.support: The review supplies the conformal equation; all torus tensor components, units, TT conditions and the root substitution are checked directly.

contents.name: §4.1, CMC equation applied to zero TT data and zero mean curvature
contents.support: The scalar equation is specialized locally; the example derives the continuum of constant solutions and the zero-mode failure of coercivity.

contents.name: §4.1 solvability qualification: not every free-data choice yields a solution
contents.support: The caveat is preserved by the item’s exact-data scope and its explicit statement that this root calculation proves no general solvability result.

contents.name: Global conformal-method classification beyond the CMC formula
contents.reason: The pair proves one exact constant-data case and one linear Fourier inverse; global Yamabe classification and general existence for arbitrary free data are expressly outside its scope.
